crisis_alert_message: HIGH - Severe LPG cylinder shortage crisis escalates: College messes forced to shut down across UP, Bihar, Delhi & Maharashtra, student bandhs spreading, commercial LPG prices hiked 25-30%, black-marketing rampant
future_emotion_forecast: Anger and Fear expected to surge by 35% in next 6 hours as more universities announce indefinite bandhs and reports of PMO emergency meeting leak on social media
narrative_summary: India is facing its worst LPG shortage in a decade in March 2026 after delayed Russian and Middle-East imports, refinery maintenance shutdowns and sudden spike in domestic + commercial demand. College hostels and messes in over 150 universities (BHU, DU, AMU, Pune University, Patna University etc.) have run out of cylinders completely – many messes closed for 3-4 days forcing students to survive on maggi, biscuits or expensive outside food. This triggered massive student bandhs, road blockades and clashes with police in Lucknow, Patna, Delhi and Mumbai. Simultaneously, commercial LPG cylinders (used by hotels, dhabas, street vendors) prices jumped from ₹1800 to ₹2400+ in open market with black-marketing at ₹3000+. Middle-class households and PG students are worst hit while opposition parties blame Centre for poor planning ahead of Holi and summer demand. Hashtags #LPGShortageIndia, #MessBandh and #LPGPriceHike are trending with millions of views on protest videos.
peoples_voice_key_takeaways: College messes in BHU, DU, Allahabad University completely shut since 5 days – students eating only biscuits and bread, demanding free emergency cylinders from state govts
Commercial LPG price hike of 25-30% has destroyed small eateries and dhabas – many closing down, vendors protesting in UP and Bihar
Black-marketing rampant in Delhi, Mumbai and Lucknow – cylinders sold at ₹2800-3500 while official rate is ₹1800, police silent
Student unions calling indefinite bandhs till LPG supply restored – clashes with police in Patna University and Pune campus
Women PG students and girls hostels worst affected – fear of safety while going out for food, many returning to villages
Opposition (Congress, RJD, AAP) accusing Modi govt of favouring Adani-Ambani refineries while ignoring public distress
Oil Ministry claims 'temporary logistics issue' but no timeline given – public demanding immediate import orders and subsidy restoration
Rural areas and small towns reporting zero supply for 10+ days, forcing families to use wood/coal chulhas again
positive_signals: Some state governments (Maharashtra, Kerala) started distributing emergency 5kg cylinders to colleges from reserve stocks
HPCL and IOCL announced special night-shift refilling at few depots in Delhi-NCR and Mumbai
NGOs and student groups organising community kitchens in affected campuses using electric induction where power available
Supreme Court mentioned the crisis in ongoing PIL – possibility of judicial intervention for priority supply
negative_signals: Widespread protests turning violent with stone pelting and lathi-charge in Lucknow University and Patna – several students injured
Health risks rising – students and families using kerosene and cow-dung cakes leading to respiratory issues reported in hospitals
Economic loss mounting – small restaurants and street vendors shutting shops, daily wage workers losing income
Trust in government at all-time low – people accusing petroleum ministry of hiding real import shortage numbers
